question: Does crossing two real brightness-matched anchor clouds and screening by connectability + a third-anchor brightness check isolate the truth-consistent pair from combinatorial junk?
hypothesis: Connectability + one brightness check isolates the truth pair from the combinatorial junk.
narrative_md: First cross of two real brightness-matched anchor clouds (no handed-in correspondence) on seed 116: crossing 1.87M pairs, connectability keeps 62.9%, the cloud-free 3rd-anchor brightness check keeps 4.26% (79,443) — a 23.5× cut retaining the truth pair. But truth is retained, not isolated (median ω-dir 91.8°, only 584 within 5°). Connectability + one brightness check is a cheap prefilter, not the discriminator. The cross consumes only observed magnitude; truth used only as a positive-control label.
